question: Fill in the blank: Grants-in-Aid to States are provided under Article ____.
solution:
The correct answer is __**275**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Grants-in-Aid to States are provided under Article **275** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Article 275 empowers the Parliament to make grants from the Consolidated Fund of India to states that require financial assistance.
 
• These grants are primarily provided to promote the welfare of Scheduled Tribes and to improve the administration of Scheduled Areas in the states.
 
• The grants are provided based on the recommendations of the Finance Commission, which assesses the financial needs of the states.
 
• Such grants are instrumental in maintaining equity and addressing regional imbalances in the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 280**

 
 
• This article establishes the **Finance Commission**, which is tasked with making recommendations to the President regarding the distribution of financial resources between the Union and the States.
 
• The Finance Commission suggests the division of tax revenue and also recommends the principles governing Grants-in-Aid under Article 275.
 
• It ensures a fair distribution of financial resources in a way that strengthens cooperative federalism.
 
 
 
• **Article 265**
 
 
• This article states that **no tax shall be levied or collected except by the authority of law**.
 
• It ensures the principle of legality in taxation, implying that taxes can only be imposed by a valid law passed by the legislature.
 
• This article safeguards citizens from arbitrary taxation and ensures fiscal accountability.
 
 
 
• **Article 110**
 
 
• It defines a **Money Bill** in the Indian Constitution.
 
• A Money Bill deals exclusively with financial matters like imposition or abolition of taxes, borrowing of money by the government, or appropriation of funds from the Consolidated Fund of India.
 
• The Speaker of the Lok Sabha has the final authority to decide whether a bill is a Money Bill or not.
